dialogues.speaker: Kanjou Commission Ashigaru
dialogues.text: Without a Travel Permit, you cannot enter or leave Ritou.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It seems if you do not have a Travel Permit, you cannot freely enter or leave the island.

dialogues.speaker: Kanjou Commission Ashigaru
dialogues.text: Without a Travel Permit, you cannot enter or leave Ritou.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It seems if you do not have a Travel Permit, you cannot freely enter or leave the island.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: According to our agreement, we'll get that Travel Permit once we <color=#00E1FFFF>deliver Miss Chisato's letter</color>, right?

dialogues.speaker: Madiha
dialogues.text: My most important partners, you're back! How did the Barking Fox's controls feel to you? Was the flight envelope broad enough?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Barking Fox wasn't difficult to control at all! It was actually pretty fun! But about that technical jargon of yours... Paimon doesn't know how to answer that!

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: Hmm... Your response would be best classified into the "user could not accurately describe their feedback" category — but that's pretty common and not a big deal at all!

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: No matter how many tries it takes, as long as you complete the test challenges without making personal modifications to the Barking Fox, then its flight performance is at the expected level!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Personal modifications?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #That sounds complicated! {NICKNAME} doesn't understand anything like that either!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Pass! Paimon doesn't fight monsters in the sky, so speed is useless to Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And if Paimon is too fast, you'll never be able to keep up!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even if Paimon races ahead and waits for you, you'll have no one to talk to, eat with, or enjoy the scenery with while catching up... And that sounds really sad!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's the point if we can't travel together!?

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: You were presented with the chance to speed through the air, yet you refuse to move forward without your companion... Ohh, I feel deeply moved by your conversation!

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: How about you two invest a bit more in me...? Hmm, yes, I think around 60 million Mora should do it!

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: I can develop... an assistive propulsion jetpack for your wind glider, and create a miniature version for you!

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: It will only take a little over a decade or so! Once it's done, you can zoom through the sky together!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eek! How did this suddenly become about Mora!? And not only are you asking us for so much, you also want us to wait a decade!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You just barely finished a small flying toy, and now you're talking about a huge device to help people fly? Can you really do that?

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: Of course! Just put your trust in me, the Phantom Toy Master!

choices.text: Then we'll use our share of the profits as the deposit!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's a great idea! Madiha said the Barking Fox will sell really well, so earning a mountain of Mora should be a piece of cake!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *ahem* Phantom Toy Master, we're your most important partners! You said the Barking Fox will sell really well, and we have such a huge cut...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe you'll be the one owing us 60 million Mora next year... maybe even more!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #But the proof's in the pudding! Make us prototypes first, and if Paimon and {NICKNAME} are satisfied, we'll consider reducing the amount you owe us!

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: Y-You're actually using business lingo to respond in kind! Curses!

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: Th-Then we'll wait until the Barking Fox goes on sale and see how it does! There's no need to worry!

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: Don't worry about what I just said! In fact, if you just forget about it, that's fine by me!

choices.text: Make a prototype first, then we can talk about investing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Really? Paimon thought it was okay...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Looks like {NICKNAME}'s become a harsh critic after testing so many people's inventions.

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: Negative feedback!? I can't believe it... Could you please tell me what's wrong?

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: Ugh, I should have expected this. Demanding users who can't even describe their problem... I don't know where to start...

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: I have to make sure our advertisements don't target such customers...

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: Uh... *ahem* That's not what I meant! Anyway, let me have a look myself! And thank you for your feedback!

choices.text: I dunno, but it just isn't good...
Maybe we should talk about you instead...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! If you call yourself the Phantom Toy Master, you must have really amazing... um... design experience? Is that how you say it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And you seem to know all about... investments? You're always talking about huge sums of Mora! You must have made a ton of money before!

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: Uh! Um! Ah!

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: E—Emotional damage!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's wrong!? You look like you're about to die of pain!

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: No! I will never die of anguish! If I am to die... I will die extremely wealthy, due to overindulging in every luxury imaginable!

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: Only the regret of missing out on a business opportunity can harm me! I even survived traveling on foot in the desert... for three whole months!

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: Those awful debt collectors who forced me to flee into the desert will never understand! But mark my words, my innovations will one day be turned into Mora!

choices.text: So you owe a lot of money.

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: No! Don't say such vulgar things! I just... I just had a lot of... unexpected expenses due to trial and error while exploring the boundlessly fantastical secrets of toys!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon finally understands Madiha's situation... and what "Phantom Toy Master" actually means...

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: You two have good instincts when it comes to people! You were willing to partner with me and provide a long-term source of capital... You'll definitely get a thousand percent return once I rise to the top!

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: So why don't we take this opportunity to give our future toy empire an additional boost...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Stop right there! If you ask us for money, we won't give you any!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! We're super broke!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, we shouldn't say that... it's not that bad! But we have a really long journey ahead of us, and we have no idea how much Mora it'll cost!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: After all, we worked hard and took a long time to earn our Mora, and we would have been starving on the streets long ago if we gave it away to just anyone...

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: Wow... Such cautious investors! Does this mean funding is drying up again...? But that's fine!

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: Just don't regret it! The earlier you invest, the higher your cut! The minimum investment will be much higher in the future!

choices.text: You're under a mountain of debt.

response.speaker: Madiha
response.text: Huh!? You still haven't gotten enough? That means flying the Barking Fox is really fun! That's great! It's a design success!

dialogues.speaker: Chatillon
dialogues.text: Distinguished guests, would you like to play Spino Blaster now?

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: No problem! Please, blast away to your heart's content!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! We imagined we were just like... gunners on a huge battleship! We were unleashing salvo after salvo, those targets didn't stand a chance!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But now that Paimon thinks about it... do real ship gunners have to aim at so many targets in such a short time, too? That's really tough...

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: Precisely so! Now you understand the original inspiration behind the game!

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: Shells don't fly in a straight line but arcs. Gunners must raise the cannon to hit faraway targets...

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: At the same time, the ship will be rocking on the waves, so the gunner must adjust the cannon vertically to compensate for the pitch and roll.

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: For all of those reasons, gunners must be extremely proficient in determining the proper elevation of the cannon barrel in order to be able to properly aim in all situations.

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: Of course, it's also essential to learn how to lead properly in order to hit fast-moving targets. The faster the target and the slower the shell, the more difficult it is to predict how much to lead.

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: That's why I invented the Crocomorph Vortex-Based Crocodilian-Armored Heavy Naval Battleship-Style Water Blasting Training Cannon! The speed and cost of ammo are both quite low.

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: By placing the cannon on a rocking, floating platform and using balloon targets, superb gunners can be quickly trained, greatly increasing the battle prowess of the entire fleet!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So this game is actually a project to train gunners!? Paimon smells a new scent in the air... and it's gunpowder!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If Idyia found out there's such a military project in Veluriyam Mirage... wouldn't she feel unsafe?

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: Relax! Lady Idyia knows all about this. I don't plan to change Veluriyam Mirage into anything resembling a battlefield.

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: Pay attention to my words! I said it was my "original" inspiration, and now it's "recreational" and not "training."

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: Far as I can tell... Fontaine's fleet doesn't need me anymore. Or rather, Fontaine has no intention to ever form another fleet like that.

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: My invention has no other purpose, so it might as well be used for something fun. At least it will bring people some happiness.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why do you sound so dejected? Did talking about Fontaine's fleet remind you of anything unpleasant?

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: Haha, nothing like that! I don't want to spoil the mood!

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: Lady Idyia gave me a precious opportunity that allows me to keep doing what I do best. As long as you're happy, I'm happy!

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: The work I talked about is all in the past! Just forget it, focus on enjoying yourself and the Crococannon!

choices.text: I think I can go a few more rounds...

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: Wonderful, seems like this game has captured your interest!

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: The basic idea is simply for you to enjoy yourself, so it isn't very difficult yet...

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: But if you get good at it and feel ready for a challenge, just be patient. I'll add some new wrinkles and twists to it as soon as possible!

choices.text: Why don't we talk about your story?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah, Paimon is curious about your past too... Why did you think about making a game out of water cannons?

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: Oh, that's simple! My old job was related to cannons.

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: A very long time ago, I was a weapon engineer for Fontaine's fleet. My wife and daughter were both excellent gunners serving on the flagship.

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: You could say my whole family is quite familiar with cannons!

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: My wife and daughter often gave me firsthand feedback. Thanks to their expertise, I became an outstanding engineer, and was elevated to work on some impressive projects.

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: I was often away from home testing weapons. Incidentally, the desert has a lot of empty spaces to test cannons and shells, so I became a frequent visitor.

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: However, in one field test, we neglected to store the shells and detonators separately, and there was a massive explosion...

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: The team suffered grievous losses. I was tossed away like a ragdoll, and I count myself lucky to have survived, though I laid in that forsaken desert in a coma for days!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th—That's horrifying!

choices.text: Your tale of tragedy has moved me to tears...

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: Yeah! So, remember, kids: safety first when handling explosives, always!

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: After that, I dragged my battered body, tracking down my injured colleagues with great difficulty, but we were lost in the desert and had to stay put for the rescue.

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: And just like that, we were forced to live in the desert. I don't know how long we survived like that, but rescue never came. After we exhausted our supplies, we thought we were done for...

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: Luckily, we stumbled across Lady Idyia! She invited us to her new home: the Veluriyam Mirage you're in now. Compared to the desert, it's a much more hospitable environment.

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: Miss Idyia also informed us about what was happening in Fontaine. Some of us got anxious and returned to Fontaine with her aid, but others felt it was meaningless to go back...

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: I, too, was depressed for a while... But to repay Miss Idyia for saving my life, I decided to use my strength to help her make the park more fun and entertaining!

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: After who knows how long, I started to miss my old work, so I decided to build this Crococannon, and a new attraction for the park...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, does that mean you've been in Veluriyam Mirage for a long time now, Mr. Chatillon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why didn't you go back to your wife and daughter? Just what did Miss Idyia tell you...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Hey, how come Mr. Chatillon is looking so gloomy all of a sudden?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Paimon still doesn't know what exactly happened, but... your Crococannon made us really happy, and will certainly do the same for other visitors too, Mr. Chatillon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you can be happy, and forget all that stuff that makes you sad!

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: You're right! I've got to get a hold of myself, and be happy! It's what they all would have wanted!

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: Every time I see the Crococannon in action, it reminds me of my daughter's favorite crocodile doll... And once she grew up, how cool she looked when operating the cannons with her mother...

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: Thank you! Your support for the Crococannon and my project means the world to me.

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: I will make this attraction even more fun! If it becomes popular, then more people will play and forget the troubles of the past!

choices.text: Although I don't know the details...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You will succeed for sure, Mr. Chatillon!

choices.text: But it's a good thing you survived.

response.speaker: Chatillon
response.text: Yes, you seem quite busy, I understand. I'll be here waiting, come back whenever you have time!

dialogues.speaker: Basima
dialogues.text: A-hmm-hmm-hmm~ Now you've played Bing-Bang Finchball, have you not? Now do you agree with me when I say that finches are the cutest?

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: Ohoho! That's true, nobody should leave after just playing one round of Finchball! Play to your heart's content!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep! Paimon couldn't tell by just reading the rules, but once Paimon started playing, Paimon found out the game was really fun!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hold the Finchball in your palm, and feel its unique round design! Then, study it closely, and you discover incredible details you never expected...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: After that, you won't be able to resist trying to recall what real finches look like, and comparing them...

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: Your reactions are amazing! This is exactly why I designed this game!

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: If this game catches on in Teyvat, it'll spark a wave of finch fever! People everywhere will want to share their lives with a precious finch by their side!

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: Perhaps there will even be finch cafes, finch taverns, and even finch hotels! That way, even those who cannot raise a finch of their own can still bask in their radiant cuteness.

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: The sheer adorableness of finches would supercharge everyone's spirits with love, people would become more patient, and the world would have fewer arguments...

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: With time, Teyvat would become a land of peace! That's why I have to work hard on this game!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now that Paimon thinks carefully about what Basima has said, it makes a lot of sense, does it not...? Pet people are usually patient and reasonable...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Finches are cute, and can be found everywhere. If more and more people fell in love with them, and raised them as pets, it would surely change their attitudes, and create an atmosphere of peaceful discussion!

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: Yes, that's absolutely what will happen! And thus, the two of you can be considered the first "Ambassadors of Finchpeace"!

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: You may freely use any of my creations, even all of Bing-bang Finchball! The only condition is that you spread the word across the world!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, who would've thought Basima had such a long-term plan for this game... Paimon's impressed!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #No problem! Finchball is safe in the hands of Paimon and {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: Great! Ambassadors of Finchpeace, we have a deal!

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: For the sake of world peace, let us shout out those words of wisdom for all of Teyvat to hear—

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: Finches are the cutest!

choices.text: Rest easy, the finches will guide our way!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It may sound a bit dramatic, but it is a distinct possibility... Pet people are usually patient and reasonable.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If more people raised finches as pets, it would surely change their attitudes, and create an atmosphere of peaceful discussion!

choices.text: I think Paimon is even cuter!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Shh, keep it down! Even Paimon... can get embarrassed sometimes!

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: Haha, this I will admit! Now that I look more closely, your floating white companion is every bit as adorable as a finch!

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: The tiny body, the carefree attitude, the fluffy white hair, the chubby round cheeks, the big watery eyes like crystals and a delightfully colorful costume with naught a speck of dust or blemish...

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: Ordinary folk like me would never encounter such a wondrous traveling companion! Honored guest, you must be one in a million... no, a billion, to have such a friend!

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: So, in the eyes of most people, perhaps we should say... "If you don't count the extraordinary Paimon, finches are the cutest!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks this conversation has gotten really weird...

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: You must take care to protect your companion! After all, many people covet that which is cute! Some of the bad ones may even try to fight you for companion...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are you saying!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can tell you have good intentions, but let Paimon set you straight on a few things—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Companions are not something that can be won in a fight! It's a bond built on mutual trust, shared experiences, going through thick and thin, shared understandings... that's what matters!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #No one can take Paimon away from {NICKNAME}! And Paimon doesn't trust easily!

choices.text: I can fight off the baddies.

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: An amazing speech! Such knowledge! I must applaud!

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: I never imagined that Paimon is not just an adorable companion, but also truly wise!

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: When I make the next game version, I shall add a new Finchball called "Companion Paimon"!

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: This new Finchball will have the ability to... lead everyone on a happy journey, progressing foward with joy, and removing all annoying obstacles!

choices.text: We only make friends with those that are Paimon-approved.
Hahaha! I truly am the blessed among the fortunate!
What is the true meaning of "cute"?

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: Yes, what exactly is "cute"? Your seemingly casual question actually brings us to essential and critical debates on definition.

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: Do certain shapes and colors form images that impact our psychology via our vision, and thus create this sensation?

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: Or do certain tones and pitches form sounds that reverberate inside us, creating a resonance with our feelings?

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: Thousands of papers can be written on the definition of "cute," and the academic world could debate it for decades...

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: Hahaha, but debates like those become a battle of academic resources! It is not reason and truth that wins, but power and position!

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: I suggest that you stay out debates like that, else you might end up like me... wasting years, losing the debate in the end, and offending an entire cafe worth of scholars...

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: Then my days at the Akademiya became a nightmare... I was dispatched into the desert with nothing but a small pack of provisions for a survey on mysterious creatures and almost died of hunger and thirst...

choices.text: I didn't know you'd tell me your life story...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can't believe that a simple debate about cuteness in the academic world could go so far...

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: I've decided to let it go. After all, with Idyia's help, I now live in the Veluriyam Mirage and can spend all my time researching cute things, free of worry and care!

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: Of course, if you wish to discuss the arcane and mysterious subject of cuteness with me, I won't be like those unscrupulous scholars who will stoop to anything just to make things difficult.

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: All I want is a friendly conversation that makes both of us happy. You are welcome back anytime!

choices.text: I guess I know how you feel...
We'll talk more about cuteness next time!

response.speaker: Basima
response.text: No problem! I believe that, when you have traveled across all of Teyvat and seen all manner of creatures, you will come back and tell me that you agree with me!

dialogues.speaker: Lafeinte
dialogues.text: Honored warriors, the shift in your auras suggests... you are supremely confident in your battle results, and your blade dance was a masterful performance for the ages!

choices.text: That's right! And we'd even like to do it again!

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: Such dauntless courage! Then please, continue to dance upon the field of battle!

choices.text: I haven't actually tried dancing yet...

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: That's just as well!

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: Even prior to you dancing the blade dance, your aura is already blindingly powerful. I cannot imagine how intimidating you will be after defeating these enemies!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks "intimidating" is a bit too much... It's not like we go around threatening people... Unless it's to give bad guys a warning!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #No matter how strong we become, {NICKNAME} is going to be just as kind, happy, super patient, and winsome as always!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And almost nobody but you has ever said we felt... intimidating or something!

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: Yes, that is exactly it! Forgive my shallow description! I remember reading something similar in novels... ahem, strategy materials from Liyue and Inazuma—

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: You have already far surpassed "using your imposing aura to suppress potential enemies and avoid combat"! You have reached an even more transcendent level!

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: It is exactly because you have no equals that you choose to appear as a completely meek and weak mortal... like even a Boar could take you out.

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: But when you run into those harboring ill intentions, you will immediately understand their intent, and acting completely casually, you will observe their every move...

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: "Whatever. But the moment you bare your weapon is the moment of your doom."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Enough with your nonsense, Mr. Lafeinte! Paimon is getting confused again...

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: Be that as it may, I have been far too impolite! Please, masters, give me one more chance that I might feast my eyes upon your most elegant posture and form!

choices.text: How'd you get here anyway, "Blade Dancer"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right... Based on how you dress, you're from... Mondstadt?

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: The nature of your question is recognition of my supreme abilities in the art of disguise.

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: In fact, I am from Fontaine, and I write novels for a living... Hmm, or should I say, apart from being the Blade Dancer, I write heroic novels for some extra pocket money in my spare time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're from Fontaine? You really don't look like it!

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: I dress like a Mondstadter because I once traveled there for a period of time. The clothes are comfortable and convenient. They conceal my identity too...

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: When there are not terrible foes with which to waltz the dance of blades, it is wise to hide your weapons and keep a low profile.

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: Or else the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, or even the Marechaussee Phantom...

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: Ahem! Or else, some strange law enforcement officer will find you, disarm you, and make sure you don't intend to harm the city.

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: They are lithe as cats, fast as the wind, and where they have passed, a unique scent of the sea and algae lingers...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are you talking about... some kind of fairy-tale creature? Sounds like an excuse for past failures!

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: Anyway, I suggest you don't mess with the law in Fontaine, they can be very difficult...

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: Of course, if you must do something in the name of conscience... then you must steel yourself in advance. You must prepare to leave Fontaine with no regrets, so as not to be arrested!

response.speaker: Lafeinte
response.text: You two... I see it clearly! You have entered the optimal state to begin the battle dance, and I should not disturb you... I look forward to another graceful performance!
